EXPERIMENT DESIGN (DESIGN ONLY — NO EXPERIMENT RUN, NO RESULTS CLAIMED)

Title: Decomposing InfLLM: How critical are dynamic context memory lookup and unit-representation choice to long-context performance?

════════════════════════════════════════
0. PRE-REGISTRATION / SOURCE-VERIFICATION STEP (must precede all constants)
════════════════════════════════════════
Because /workspace contains no InfLLM paper, code, or checkpoints (verified: only task.json exists; filesystem search found no InfLLM artifacts), every architectural constant below is defined RELATIVE to the published paper's reported defaults (InfLLM, Xiao et al., arXiv:2402.04617) and is labeled [SRC-VERIFY]. Before any design constant is frozen, the following must be read from the paper and official repository and recorded in a pre-registration memo:
  V1. Block (unit) size, activation-window size (number of always-attended neighbor blocks), and top-k blocks retrieved per query. [UNVERIFIED — all ablation levels are expressed as multipliers/fractions of these reported defaults, never as absolute numbers presented as facts.]
  V2. The unit-representation computation: exact pooling/projection of block tokens into the lookup key. [UNVERIFIED]
  V3. The retrieval scoring function and whether retrieval keys and the stored KV cache are separable code paths. [UNVERIFIED]
  V4. Whether memory update is append-only or involves recomputation/re-encoding of older blocks. [UNVERIFIED — gates the optional Arm C, §4.]
  V5. Which base LLM checkpoint and context length the paper reports, and the training-free inference recipe details. [UNVERIFIED]
The pre-registration memo is committed before ablation implementation begins; any discrepancy between this design and the verified source updates the design, not the source.

════════════════════════════════════════
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND HYPOTHESES
════════════════════════════════════════
Q: How critical are (A) dynamic context memory lookup and (B) the choice of unit representations to InfLLM's performance across long-context tasks?
H-A (lookup criticality): replacing dynamic learned retrieval with fixed/heuristic selection (A2) and random selection (A3) monotonically degrades performance, with the largest degradation at deep (far-from-window) positions.
H-B (representation criticality): degrading unit representations (B2 token-mean pooling; B3 shuffled/random) degrades performance primarily by corrupting retrieval precision; B3 should collapse toward the sliding-window floor.
H-I (interaction): the two factors are approximately independent (no compensatory interaction); the mixed cells test this.
Primary estimand: the fraction-of-gap recovered (§6), i.e., how much of the gap between the no-memory floor and the reference InfLLM (or full-attention ceiling, where feasible) is attributable to each component.

════════════════════════════════════════
2. MODEL AND INFERENCE SETUP [ASSUMPTION-BASED FEASIBILITY BASIS]
════════════════════════════════════════
REPRESENTATIVE ASSUMPTION (explicitly labeled; not a verified fact): a 7B-class open-weight LLM as InfLLM's backbone, evaluation-only (frozen weights, no fine-tuning), running on a single multi-GPU node (representative budget: 8×80GB GPUs, e.g., A100/H100 class). All ablations operate on the SAME frozen checkpoint and decoding settings (greedy or fixed-temperature sampling; identical prompt templates) so parameter counts match by construction. Any variant that would introduce new parameters is either implemented training-free or given a parameter-matched twin (§5). SCALING NOTE: costs scale roughly linearly in parameters for inference time and linearly in context length for memory/KV storage; a 13B model ≈ 2× the per-token cost of 7B (same memory topology), a 2× larger block/top-k doubles retrieved-attention cost quadratically in attended tokens (attention is O(attended²) per query). Budget rows in §7 should be rescaled accordingly.

════════════════════════════════════════
3. BENCHMARK SCOPE (per researcher decision)
════════════════════════════════════════
Three task families, LongBench-style QA as the primary axis:
  T1. Document/multi-hop QA (primary): one LongBench-style multi-document QA task (e.g., HotpotQA-style multi-doc or Qasper) — measures end-task quality under realistic retrieval needs. [Task family choice per researcher decision; exact dataset named in pre-registration memo.]
  T2. Retrieval: needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) with depth-resolved accuracy curves at multiple context depths (near-window, mid, deep/far). Deep positions are the regime where dynamic lookup should matter most — a targeted diagnostic.
  T3. Streaming perplexity: continuous-stream language modeling (PG19-style concatenation) at lengths beyond the training context window; per-position perplexity split by distance-from-window bands. This measures the mechanism without task-format confounds.
Rationale for the trio: T3 is a clean mechanistic measure (no formatting variance); T2 isolates positional retrieval ability; T1 is the ecological end-task. Together they span the "across long-context tasks" requirement with one task per family (feasibility-driven prioritization, per researcher decision).

════════════════════════════════════════
4. CONDITION GRID (2 factors, full factorial + anchors + optional arm)
════════════════════════════════════════
Factor A — memory lookup:
  A1. Original dynamic learned retrieval (reference). [Level = paper default top-k.]
  A2. Fixed/heuristic selection: same NUMBER of blocks as A1, chosen by a heuristic (recency + deterministic stride over the history). No learned scoring.
  A3. Random selection: same number of blocks, sampled uniformly (≥3 seeds). Lower-bound control for the lookup factor.
Factor B — unit representations:
  B1. Original unit representation (reference). [Computation per V2.]
  B2. Token-mean pooling: replace the learned/derived representation with a simple mean over the block's tokens. A "reasonable but simpler" alternative.
  B3. Shuffled/random embeddings: permute representations across blocks within the document (and/or Gaussian-noise them). Joint degradation of lookup keys and any representation-derived stored state — a lower-bound control. [LIMITATION, per researcher decision: if V3 shows keys and KV cache are separable code paths, a conditional refinement splits B3 into (B3a) degrade lookup keys only vs. (B3b) degrade stored KV only; otherwise B3 stays joint and is reported as a limitation.]
Core grid: {A1,A2,A3} × {B1,B2,B3} = 9 cells.
Anchors (not part of the factorial):
  F. Sliding-window-only baseline (no retrieved memory at all; activation window only) — absolute floor for the gap-fraction.
  C. Full-attention reference at lengths where compute permits (e.g., within ~32K–128K, per budget) — ceiling anchor; not feasible at streaming lengths (noted).
Optional Arm C (CONDITIONAL on V4): if source verification shows memory update involves recomputation/re-encoding of older blocks, add a freeze-vs-refresh ablation: (C1) freeze representations at block creation vs. (C2) refresh at retrieval time, crossed with A1B1 and A1B2. If V4 shows append-only updating, Arm C is dropped and the "dynamic" factor is interpreted purely as selection dynamics. This arm is explicitly optional and triggered only by source evidence. [Per researcher decision.]
Memory-capacity robustness axis: each factorial cell runs at multiple memory capacities — top-k ∈ {small, medium, large} (e.g., {0.25×, 1×, 4×} of the paper default [SRC-VERIFY]) and, for a subset of cells (A1B1, A2B1, A1B3, F), block size ∈ {0.5×, 1×, 2×} of default. This tests whether component criticality grows or shrinks with memory budget.

════════════════════════════════════════
5. CONTROLS (to isolate effects)
════════════════════════════════════════
  1. Matched attention/token budget: every cell uses the same activation-window size and the same NUMBER of retrieved blocks per query (A2/A3 match A1's count; B3 shuffles but does not change counts). This ensures performance differences are not compute differences; §7's cost table verifies empirically.
  2. Matched parameters: all cells use the same frozen checkpoint; representation variants (B2) are computed from the same backbone activations with no new trainable parameters. If any variant would add parameters, it is either made training-free or given a parameter-matched twin; recorded in the memo.
  3. Identical data and prompts: same documents, same needle placements, same seeds for data order across cells; only the mechanism under test varies.
  4. Randomness control: A3 and B3 run with ≥3 seeds (selection seed / shuffle seed); A1, A2, F, C are deterministic, so seeds only quantify data-level variance there.
  5. Position stratification: NIAH needles and streaming perplexity are stratified by distance-from-window bands, so lookup effects are localized where the mechanism should matter (deep positions) vs. where they shouldn't (near-window, which should be ~unchanged across A-conditions — a built-in negative control).
  6. Sanitation check: A3B3 ≈ F (sliding-window floor) is a validity check; a large deviation indicates an implementation leak.

════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
════════════════════════════════════════
Metrics:
  • T1: task-native EM/F1 (or task accuracy) per document-length bin.
  • T2: NIAH accuracy overall AND depth-resolved (accuracy as a function of needle depth; summarized by area-under-depth-curve and deep-band accuracy).
  • T3: per-position perplexity, summarized by mean perplexity in distance bands {near, mid, far} and perplexity-vs-length curves.
  • All: efficiency metrics (tokens attended per query, wall-clock latency, memory footprint) — used for the §7 cost table, not for performance claims.
Attribution statistic — fraction-of-gap recovered (FG):
  FG(component) = (A1B1 − ablated cell) / (A1B1 − F), computed per task and averaged with task weights fixed a priori (equal weights across the three tasks as primary; per-task FG reported alongside).
  • FG_A = FG(A2B1) and FG(A3B1) → lookup criticality (two doses: heuristic and random).
  • FG_B = FG(A1B2) and FG(A1B3) → representation criticality.
  • Additivity check: |FG(A2B3) − (FG_A2 + FG_B3)| tests interaction; report with CI.
  Interpretation bands (pre-declared): FG ≥ 0.5 "critical contributor"; 0.2 ≤ FG < 0.5 "material"; FG < 0.2 "minor". Bands are interpretive conventions, declared before data.
Statistical treatment:
  • T1/T2: per-item paired comparisons against A1B1 (same items across cells); report paired bootstrap 95% CIs over items (10K resamples) for each Δ and FG.
  • T2 depth curves: per (depth-band × item) paired bootstrap; also a pre-registered contrast: deep-band Δ(A1B1−A2B1) > near-band Δ (tests the positional mechanism claim).
  • T3: streaming evaluation has high serial autocorrelation and segment-level variance [EXPECTED VARIANCE NOTE]; use segment-block bootstrap (blocks = concatenated documents) rather than token-level CIs; ≥3 evaluation passes with different stream orders if the corpus allows, to separate corpus variance from mechanism variance.
  • Seeds: A3/B3 variance estimated from ≥3 seeds; seed variance pooled into the bootstrap as an additional variance component (hierarchical bootstrap).
  • Multiplicity: Holm correction across the pre-declared primary contrasts (FG_A via A2B1, FG_B via A1B2, and the deep-band contrast); all other comparisons reported as exploratory.
  • Power/robustness note: with typical LongBench-style task sizes (hundreds of items) and paired designs, the design targets detecting FG differences ≥0.1 at 80% power under conservative item-level variance; if a task's item count is smaller, power is re-estimated in the pre-registration memo and that task's FG is reported with correspondingly wider CIs. Streaming tasks typically need fewer passes but wider block bootstrap CIs; this is the dominant variance source and is flagged up front rather than discovered later.

════════════════════════════════════════
7. FEASIBILITY AND PER-CELL EFFICIENCY/COST TABLE (template to verify matched-budget claim)
════════════════════════════════════════
Every cell logs, per benchmark: (i) mean tokens attended per query (window + k×block), (ii) prefill tokens, (iii) wall-clock latency per 1K queries, (iv) peak memory (GB), (v) total GPU-hours. The design's matched-budget claim is verified if (i) is equal across cells within ±2%; a deviation is reported and the affected comparison is flagged. Representative cost envelope (7B-class, 8×80GB node, ASSUMPTION): T1 (~hundreds of docs × up to ~128K ctx) and T2 (grid of depths × context lengths up to the model's supported extrapolation length) are the cheap cells — single-digit GPU-hours per cell; T3 streaming at ~1M-token streams × N streams is the expensive axis — order tens of GPU-hours per cell, so T3 runs the factorial only at the medium capacity level, with the capacity sweep on T3 restricted to the subset named in §4. Full grid estimate (9 cells + 2 anchors + capacity sweep): order 100–300 GPU-hours at the 7B assumption; roughly linear in parameter count and super-linear in streaming length (attention over retrieved tokens). If budget is smaller, the pre-declared priority order is: T2 depth curves at default capacity → T1 at default capacity → T3 subset → capacity sweeps.

════════════════════════════════════════
8. ASSUMPTIONS (consequential; all UNVERIFIED against local sources)
════════════════════════════════════════
  AS1. Original InfLLM checkpoints and the training-free recipe are publicly available. [UNVERIFIED]
  AS2. Ablations are evaluation-only on a frozen model (matches InfLLM's training-free design; keeps parameters matched). [UNVERIFIED]
  AS3. The top-k retrieval step is pluggable (can be swapped without altering the pipeline). [UNVERIFIED]
  AS4. Representative compute: 7B-class model, single 8×80GB node, ~100–300 GPU-hours for the full grid. [ASSUMPTION for feasibility framing; rescaling rules in §2/§7.]
  AS5. LongBench-style QA + NIAH + PG19-style streaming are acceptable proxies for "long-context tasks"; exact datasets named at pre-registration. [RESEARCHER-CONFIRMED at family level.]
  AS6. Equal task weighting in the primary FG estimand. [Analytic choice, declared a priori.]
LIMITATIONS:
  L1. B3 is a joint degradation of lookup keys and any representation-derived stored state; keys/KV separability [V3] is unverified, so representation-vs-storage effects cannot be fully separated unless the conditional refinement (§4, B3a/B3b) is triggered by source evidence.
  L2. Full-attention ceiling is not feasible at streaming lengths; gap-fractions there are normalized to the sliding-window floor only.
  L3. All architectural constants are relative to reported defaults pending V1–V5; if verification contradicts the sketched mechanism (e.g., retrieval is not per-query but per-block), the grid is revised before implementation — the attribution logic (matched-count, matched-budget, anchors) is unchanged.
  L4. No experiments were executed and no results are claimed; every performance expectation in §1 is a hypothesis, not a finding.
  L5. Design-only environment: /workspace held only task.json (no track.md, no code); all source-derived details await the pre-registration memo.
